Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-08-20 | AMZN | Underweight | -1.5% | -2.6% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN: trim into strength to roughly 55–60% of a standard allocation (hard cap 65% while the FCF gap is open), and treat this as a de-risking plus conditional re-entry — not an exit and not a short. Work sell limits in the 263.5–266.5 confluence (falling 10 EMA 263.67, 8/19 high 266.40); if AMZN does not trade there within five sessions, or fails to reclaim that zone within two sessions, complete the trim on a close below 259.45 (8/20 swing low). Do not add at $260.11 — the bull's own defined entry (249–252) sits 3.5–4.3% lower. De-risk the residual on a close below 257.73 to ~45–50%, on a decisive close below 249.32 (50 SMA) to 30–35%, and exit what remains on a close below 238.30 (200 SMA). Re-enter only in conditional halves: 10–15% on a daily close back above 249.32 with the MACD histogram improving, 10–15% on a close above 266.40 on >45M shares with the histogram turning positive; add more only after a reclaim of the 272.05 VWMA. Size so a gap through the stop is a bad day, not a bad year. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The bear case wins, and it wins on arithmetic rather than rhetoric — most decisively because the bull's load-bearing fact was inverted. The bull argued that "$161.4B of TTM operating cash flow, +33.3%, is growing faster than the capex being deployed against it." It is not: capex is +60.7% against OCF +33.3%, a ~27-point gap, with capex/revenue moving 19.2% → 27.0% in a year. Corrected, the FCF picture is what the bear described — −$11.6B TTM versus +$13.5B a year earlier, and −$27.0B in H1 before $39.8B of acquisitions and $49.3B of securities purchases. The bull never repaired the error; he pivoted to liquidity and 21x interest coverage, which nobody disputed and which answers solvency, not the direction of travel. That single correction is what forces the rating from Overweight/Hold down to Underweight.

The second and third legs are the ones the bull failed to neutralize even after conceding them. The Q2 operating line is genuinely the best number in the filing — revenue +19.6% accelerating from +16.6%, operating income $27.5B at +43.2%, margin 13.7% (+231bp), G&A −6%, inventory flat — and it is why this is not a Sell. But the bear's offset is mechanical: D&A +31.3%, D&A/revenue +90bp to 10.0%, against only ~45bp of gross-margin expansion, while capex runs at roughly $217B annualized versus ~$80B of annualized D&A. Two-thirds of the depreciation on the assets producing the current margin has not yet arrived; you cannot extrapolate 231bp of margin expansion as structural when the forward cost is arriving at ~2.7x the current run-rate. The bull called this "noise in the P&L"; it is the forward cost of the strategy he is enthusing about. Earnings quality compounds the problem: 64% of Q2 net income came from a model-marked revaluation of a $122.3B non-marketable stake (up 655% in six months, ~11% of assets, roughly a quarter of book equity), plus a separate $38.1B AOCI increase — and the package discloses neither the identity nor the valuation inputs of that stake. The bull asks investors to ignore the gap rather than resolve it. For a name whose premium multiple has always been underwritten by clean cash earnings, that changes what "earnings" means for valuation purposes.

Fourth, the balance sheet changed character while the bull quoted a snapshot: debt nearly doubled to $133.0B in six months, interest expense +155% ($516M → $1,314M), $96.3B of operating lease liabilities ($116.4B undiscounted), $13.5B of finance leases, current ratio 1.03x, and $650.0B of contractual obligations with $78.1B due inside twelve months. The bull's "if demand shows up, that's a revenue backlog" is a category error — these are Amazon's commitments to pay others, with no disclosed matching $650B of customer contracts. All three risk analysts accepted this funding/quality evidence; only their execution differed.

Fifth, the tape, where the bull's case is internally contradictory. He defended buying at $260.11 while his own setup — long 249–252 at the rising 50 SMA, stop 244.50 — sits 3.5–4.3% below spot, and his own work says "no edge at 260.11": RSI 50.92, price pinned on the Bollinger mid-band 260.05, MACD histogram −1.24 and widening since the 8/17 bearish crossover, 10 EMA falling at 263.67. The closing-basis highs run 284.02 → 278.09 → 266.40 → 263.84, price closed below the entire 7/31 session range, the 8/19 bounce to 265.84 failed on 8/20 with a close in the bottom ~14% of the range, and the only high-volume session in the last six was the 8/17 down day at 43.9M. The 10 EMA (263.67), 8/19 high (266.40) and VWMA (272.05) form triple-confirmed overhead supply. Rising 50/200 SMAs and a widening golden cross are lagging, and with the 200 SMA 8.4% below spot they are distance, not support.

Where the bull holds ground, and why the rating is Underweight rather than Sell: revenue is accelerating, overhead leverage is real, inventory is flat, $176.1B of liquidity and ~21x coverage are genuine, and the long-term trend is not broken — the bear conceded all of it and his own posture was "stand aside at this price," not short. With the 200 SMA 8.4% below spot, a fresh short has poor reward-to-risk (1.1–1.8:1 by the technical work). On sizing I side with the neutral analyst over both extremes: the conservative's 40–50% residual and 257.73-to-30% trigger are too punitive given a rising 50 SMA, contracting ATR (nine straight contractions, 9.948 → 7.746) and a 257.73 level that sits only ~0.9% below spot, well inside one ATR; the aggressive's 60% residual with a blind 249–252 limit and a 244.50 stop (under one ATR) pre-commits capital to a support test that has not happened. The record supports the middle: prior AMZN Underweights that over-de-risked an intact primary trend cost +12% to +22% of five-day alpha, while the more recent measured trims (−0.1% alpha on 8/12) were neutral rather than damaging — so conviction rides on the size of the trim and the height of the re-entry bar, not on a directional short or a zeroed position.

What would change the call. Upward toward Hold/Overweight: TTM FCF inflecting positive or the capex-vs-OCF gap closing; D&A/revenue stabilizing at ~10.0% with gross margin holding or expanding (margin expansion proving structural rather than pre-depreciation); a volume-confirmed close above 266.40 on >45M shares with a positive histogram, then a reclaim of 272.05; or AWS segment revenue/margin actually disclosed. Downward toward Sell: a decisive close below 249.32 with the FCF gap still open, further debt issuance or interest expense annualizing above ~$6B, or any markdown in the $122.3B equity book — and because that last risk arrives as a gap, exposure must already be small when it happens.

Explicit gaps I am not underwriting: no AWS segment revenue or operating income anywhere in the materials, so both sides' AWS arguments are inference from headlines; no identity or valuation inputs for the $122.3B non-marketable stake; no explanation of the $38.1B AOCI swing; no organic-versus-acquired revenue split; the news sample is incomplete (20 of 173 records, 19 on one day) and the one price-direction datapoint attributes 8/19 strength to sector beta, not company news; and no portfolio, holdings or cash context was provided, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation.

**Price Target**: 252.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of −2.6% (raw −1.5%) is consistent with the Underweight call, but five sessions is far too short to judge a 3–6 month thesis built on FCF and depreciation arithmetic. What the window does support is the tape leg: overhead supply at the 263.67 10 EMA / 266.40 confluence capped price and the widening negative MACD histogram resolved down, while the FCF gap and D&A arguments remain entirely untested. The lesson is execution, not direction — with price only ~0.9% above the 259.45 trigger and inside one ATR, waiting on 263.5–266.5 sell limits that price never revisited meant the trim happened lower, so next time complete at least half the trim at market when the confluence sits more than one ATR above spot on a deteriorating histogram.

[2026-08-19 | AMZN | Underweight | -2.1% | -1.7% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Underweight: trim 40–50% of a full single-name exposure now, taking a standard 5% position to roughly 2.5–3.0% of portfolio. Execute the first tranche at/near the $265.84 close rather than waiting for a rally, and leave a working limit in the $271.58–$272.65 VWMA/supply shelf for any residual strength. Do not initiate a new long and do not short at $265.84; the tactical overlay is optional and trigger-only on a daily close below $257.73 on >40M shares, capped at half the trader's maximum (≤0.25–0.5% portfolio risk, stop $266.50) or expressed as a defined-risk put. De-risk the residual on closes below $257.73 (~25% of standard) and $249.00 (structural failure, $238.22 target); restore in two steps — 3.5–4.0% only on a close above $272.65 on ≥48M shares with the MACD histogram recrossing zero, full weight only after the Q3 capex/margin/D&A/deferred-revenue/mark checks. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the late-October print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not in dispute: the Research Manager, the trader, and all three risk seats converge on reducing AMZN, and the aggressive analyst is right that this is the rare debate where the "aggressive" action and the prudent action are the same trade. What decided the call is that the aggressive analyst won the two arguments that set the multiple, the conservative won execution and gap risk, and the neutral won the structure of the response.

The aggressive analyst wins on cash-flow and earnings quality, and neither colleague refuted it. TTM free cash flow is –$11.6B against +$13.5B a year earlier; H1 FCF is –$27.0B against a $173B TTM capex run-rate; Q2 D&A is only 37% of Q2 capex and TTM D&A only 43% of TTM capex, so the 1.3–2.0 point annual margin headwind is still ahead — the "Q2 already absorbed it" defense fails because Q2 D&A depreciates prior-year assets, not the current surge. Cash taxes of $4.0B on $120.7B of H1 pretax income flatter the $161.4B OCF headline by roughly $30B, leaving a mid-30s core multiple on core EPS near $1.96 rather than the reported $5.75. Lease-adjusted the balance sheet is roughly –$66.7B net debt, not net cash, and the $122.3B non-marketable equity book — up 655% in six months, ~11% of assets, driving $62.8B of H1 pre-tax upward adjustments — is correlated beta to the same AI narrative that supports the multiple, not free optionality. Negative FCF plus a mid-30s core multiple plus no buyback and no dividend is no margin of safety.

The tape reinforces the trim rather than refuting it. AMZN at $265.84 closed below the $271.91 VWMA, so the dollar-weighted buyer of the last ~20 sessions is underwater — precisely why every rally from 08-04 to 08-11 died in the $271.58–$278.09 shelf. The lower-high sequence $287.20 → $280.14 → $266.40 is intact, the 08-17 MACD bear cross is still in force (histogram –0.8817, line down five sessions from 8.43 to 4.81), the 08-19 reversal printed 35.76M shares against a ~48.2M average (~71%), and an unfilled gap from roughly $231.06 to $265.00 sits directly beneath price. A bullish outside day on 71% volume into a shelf that has rejected three times is a bounce, not a reversal.

But the aggressive overreaches in three places and the conservative and neutral are right to cut him back. The anatomy is not bearish enough for a directional short: price is 11.59% above a rising 200 SMA ($238.22), 6.8% above a rising 50 SMA ($249.00) the pullback never tested, RSI is 55.64 mid-range with no confirmed divergence, the MACD line is still positive at 4.81, and the 08-19 session held the higher low ($258.58 vs $257.73) and reclaimed the 10 EMA ($264.46). The overlay as proposed is not "cheap convexity": with ATR at 7.86 (2.95% of spot) the $266.50 stop is only ~1.1 ATR above the $257.73 trigger, so a stop-run through the $258.58–$259.45 confluence is as likely as the gap-fill — it is a new volatility exposure and must be half-sized or expressed as a defined-risk put. And treating the missing Form 4 data as a bearish certainty is wrong; it is an information gap, and the correct response to an unknown is less exposure, not a second way to lose money.

I side with the conservative and neutral on execution: AMZN gapped $235.50 → $265.00 overnight in late July, and the largest identified tail — a markdown against a $122.3B model-valued book — is exactly a gap event that will not politely print $257.73 so a trigger can fire. So the reduction does not depend on reaching $271.58; the first tranche executes near the $265.84 close with a limit left in the shelf. Where I side with the neutral against the conservative is restoration: requiring a $272.65/48M close plus every fundamental gate plus insider review before any weight returns converts a tactical underweight into permanent avoidance of a business still compounding operating income at +43.2% on a 13.7% margin with +19.6% revenue growth. The two-stage gate is the correct compromise.

That is why the rating is Underweight and not Sell. A Sell abandons a franchise whose operating engine is accelerating and whose primary structure — rising 50 and 200 SMA, uninterrupted higher low — has not failed, and the record is unambiguous that full exits and heavy underweights on AMZN in this cycle (07-22 through 07-30) cost between 12% and 22% of five-day alpha. The mirror lessons are live too: the 08-12 Underweight produced –0.1% alpha and the 08-11 Hold –4.3%, and the cross-ticker AAPL lesson warns specifically that an Underweight whose falsification level sits only ~2.6% above spot (here $272.65 vs $265.84) has poor expectancy unless a real core is retained. Keeping 2.5–3.0% rather than exiting respects both.

What would change it. Upward: a close above $272.65 on ≥48M shares with the MACD histogram recrossing zero restores 3.5–4.0%; full weight requires Q3 capex flat or down, operating margin ≥13.7% with D&A/revenue ≥10.5%, deferred revenue growing off the flat ~$24.9B (against receivables +30.1% on revenue +19.6%), and non-marketable equity flat or positive. Downward: a close below $257.73 on >40M takes the core to ~25% of standard and legitimizes the half-sized overlay; a close below $249.00 confirms structural failure toward $238.22, at which point the thesis is being validated by price and the residual should be re-underwritten, not defended.

Explicit gaps I am not underwriting: no Form 4/insider data, so insider behavior cannot be scored in either direction; no AWS segment revenue, margin or backlog, so the AWS thesis and the demand side of a $173B capex program are unvalidated; no organic-versus-acquired revenue split despite a large acquisition program; no consensus, peer comps or valuation multiples, so the 34–36x core multiple is report-derived arithmetic rather than a computed screen; and no portfolio, holdings or cash context, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation and should flex with whatever other AI-capex exposure the caller already carries.

**Price Target**: 252.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
Five-day alpha of -1.7% (raw -2.1% vs SPY) means the Underweight call was directionally right, but five sessions cannot validate a 3–6 month thesis built on FCF and core earnings — treat it as tape confirmation only. What it supports is the execution half of the argument: refusing to wait for the $271.58 shelf and taking the first tranche at the $265.84 close, with the lower-high sequence and sub-VWMA close playing out as written; the FCF/D&A/core-multiple case remains untested until the Q3 print. Lesson for next time: when the falsification level sits only ~2.6% above spot, the trim's alpha arrives fast and is easily mistaken for thesis confirmation — keep the at-market first tranche, but pre-commit to judging the fundamental leg only at the scheduled catalyst.

[2026-08-18 | AMZN | Overweight | +0.6% | +0.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Build AMZN toward 1.0-1.1x a standard allocation (moderating the 1.2-1.3x initially proposed) via a staged, confirmation-gated entry.
